qt: to the Commission Nikola Minchev (Renew) Subject:
Unresolved concerns regarding the composition of Bulgaria’s Supreme Judicial Council

Successive Commission Rule of Law Reports1 have raised long-standing concerns about the composition of Bulgaria’s Supreme Judicial Council (SJC), more specifically its Judges’ Chamber, noting that judges elected by their peers do not constitute a majority in this chamber. This raises questions about the disproportionate influence of the parliamentary majority and the Prosecutor General over the whole SJC. The constitutional amendments adopted in December 20232 sought to address this imbalance. However, following the Constitutional Court of Bulgaria’s ruling of July 20243, the previous framework remained in place. The issue remains unsolved, despite the change in parliamentary majority following Bulgaria’s parliamentary elections in April 2026 and its stated commitment to judicial reform and combating corruption. In the light of these persistent challenges to the protection of judicial independence and the rule of law, what additional concrete measures does the Commission intend to take to ensure that Bulgaria brings the composition and functioning of the Judges’ Chamber of the SJC into line with European standards on judicial independence?

2026 Rule of Law Report, Country Chapter on the rule of law situation in Bulgaria (SWD/2026/0902), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52026SC0902&qid=1793091216642. https://www.parliament.bg/en/bills/ID/165057. https://www.constcourt.bg/en/act-9861.
